sections.h2: Matching Japan's matcha would take 0.29% of India's tea and 0.58% of Assam's

chart.title: Japan's whole matcha output needs just 0.58% of Assam's tea crop
chart.sub: Share of the national or state tea crop needed to match Japan's matcha output, %.
chart.source: Tea Board; MAFF via trade press; computed in the post.

sections.means: Volume is not the constraint: about four million kg of matcha needs under one per cent of India's tea crop.
sections.todo: Plant Camellia sinensis cultivars selected for matcha rather than shading existing assamica bushes, since cultivar is the real constraint.

sections.h2: Tencha auction price doubled to ₹6,539/kg, and India's first lot sold at 46% of it

chart.title: India's first matcha lot sold at under half the Japanese tencha price
chart.source: MAFF via trade press; Chota Tingrai Tea Estate auction result.

sections.means: Auction prices roughly doubled in 2026, and India's first commercial lot fetched ₹3,000/kg, about 46 per cent of the tencha price.
sections.todo: Decide early whether India sells matcha as an ingredient commodity or builds a grade and origin claim, since that branding choice is hard to reverse.

sections.h2: Powdered green tea now makes up 69% of Japan's green tea exports by weight

chart.title: Powdered green tea is now 69% of Japan's green tea exports

sections.means: The powdered category that was once a ceremonial niche is now most of Japan's green tea export volume.
sections.todo: Treat bulk powder as the export format to plan for, since powdered tea is already the bulk of Japan's green tea trade.
